title: Document accepted `WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE` meanings in wp-config.
body:
## Issue Description

The wp-config docs for `WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE` provides information on the valid values for the constant but does not provide any definition of what these values mean.

It would be helpful to extend the docs to provide these definitions as they are currently hidden away on a make/core post.


## URL of the Page with the Issue

https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/wp-config-php/#wp-environment-type

## Section of Page with the issue

`WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE`

## Why is this a problem?

Without definitions it is unclear which of the accepted values is best used for a particular circumstance.

## Suggested Fix

> WordPress supports four environment types:
> 
> * `production` (default): a live site connected to and reachable via the internet,
> * `staging`: a non-production staging environment connected to and reachable via the the internet
> * `development`: a non-production development environment connected to and reachable via the internet
> * `local`: a non-production development environment that can reach the internet but is **not** reachable via the internet
> 
> `WP_DEBUG` is automatically enabled for sites set to either the `development` or `local` environment types.
> 
> For environments reachable via the internet the Application Passwords feature requires the site be served over a secure HTTPS connection. For `local` environments the Application Passwords feature will work over insecure HTTP connections.

title: Trailing space in `FTP_PLUGIN_DIR` constant name on wp-config.php page
body:
## Issue Description

The `FTP_PLUGIN_DIR` example has a space inside the constant name.

## URL of the Page with the Issue

https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/wp-config-php/#wordpress-upgrade-constants

## Section of Page with the issue

WordPress Upgrade Constants

## Why is this a problem?

`define( 'FTP_PLUGIN_DIR ', ... )` defines a constant called `FTP_PLUGIN_DIR ` (with a space), so the real `FTP_PLUGIN_DIR` is never set. Anyone who copies the example gets a setting that silently does nothing.

## Suggested Fix

```php
define( 'FTP_PLUGIN_DIR', '/path/to/wordpress/wp-content/plugins/' );
```

title: `WP_DEBUG` is commented out in the Fatal Error Handler example on wp-config.php page
body:
## Issue Description

In the example, the comment and the `WP_DEBUG` define are on the same line, so the define is commented out.

## URL of the Page with the Issue

https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/wp-config-php/#wp-disable-fatal-error-handler

## Section of Page with the issue

WP_DISABLE_FATAL_ERROR_HANDLER

## Why is this a problem?

Current code:

```php
define( 'WP_DISABLE_FATAL_ERROR_HANDLER', true ); // 5.2 and later define( 'WP_DEBUG', true );
```

Everything after `//` is ignored, so `WP_DEBUG` is never enabled, even though the section is about showing errors.

## Suggested Fix

```php
define( 'WP_DISABLE_FATAL_ERROR_HANDLER', true ); // 5.2 and later
define( 'WP_DEBUG', true );
define( 'WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY', true );
```

title: Clarify theme ZIP file structure for updates
body:
The current documentation (https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/work-with-themes/#adding-new-themes-using-the-administration-screens and https://learn.wordpress.org/lesson/updating-your-theme/) implicitly assumes that a theme's ZIP file will contain a single root folder and that all theme files will reside within that folder. This is a common and well-known best practice among experienced developers. However, it is not explicitly stated as a hard requirement (or I'm unable to find this requirement in the docs).

This lack of explicit documentation can lead to a specific bug, as demonstrated in the Trac ticket https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/63737. When a user attempts to update a theme via ZIP upload, if the theme's files are at the root of the ZIP archive (instead of being inside a containing folder), a previous failed update attempt (e.g., trying to upload the theme ZIP through the plugin installer) can cause subsequent, correct update attempts to fail. WordPress, in this scenario, creates a new directory (e.g., my-theme-1) instead of overwriting the existing theme folder, breaking the update process.

Proposed Change:
Add a new, clear, and prominent section to the relevant documentation that explicitly states the correct ZIP file structure for themes. This should be added to both developer-facing and user-facing documentation.

## Issue Description
The Header Requirements page of the Plugin Handbook has several small grammar and punctuation errors, mostly in the opening sentence and the Header Fields list.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/plugin-basics/header-requirements/

## Section of Page with the issue
The introductory paragraph, the Header Fields list (Plugin URI, Description, Network and Update URI), and the sentence introducing the second code example.

## Why is this a problem?
The opening sentence is ungrammatical ("should include header comment what tells WordPress that a file is a plugin"). It is the first thing readers see on the page, and it is also used as the page's meta description, so it shows up in search results and link previews. The other items are smaller inconsistencies and redundancies that make the text harder to read.

## Suggested Fix
**1. Introductory paragraph** (missing article, "what" instead of "that", "a file" instead of "the file")
Current: the main PHP file should include header comment what tells WordPress that a file is a plugin and provides information about the plugin.
Suggested: the main PHP file should include a header comment that tells WordPress that the file is a plugin and provides information about the plugin.

**2. Plugin URI** (says the URL "should be" unique, then that it "must be" unique)
Current: The home page of the plugin, which should be a unique URL, preferably on your own website. This *must be unique* to your plugin. You cannot use a WordPress.org URL here.
Suggested: The home page of the plugin, preferably on your own website. This *must be unique* to your plugin. You cannot use a WordPress.org URL here.

**3. Description** (the same admin screen is called the "Plugins list" in the Plugin Name field)
Current: as displayed in the Plugins section in the WordPress Admin.
Suggested: as displayed in the Plugins list in the WordPress Admin.

**4. Network** (unnecessary comma: both verbs share the same subject)
Current: Can only be set to *true*, and should be left out when not needed.
Suggested: Can only be set to *true* and should be left out when not needed.

**5. Update URI** (missing article; the Requires Plugins field already says "read the related dev note")
Current: For more info read related [dev note](https://make.wordpress.org/core/2021/06/29/introducing-update-uri-plugin-header-in-wordpress-5-8/).
Suggested: For more info read the related [dev note](https://make.wordpress.org/core/2021/06/29/introducing-update-uri-plugin-header-in-wordpress-5-8/).


**6. Sentence before the second code example** (restrictive clause, so "that" rather than "which")
Current: Here's another example which allows file-level PHPDoc DocBlock as well as WordPress plugin file headers:
Suggested: Here's another example that allows file-level PHPDoc DocBlock as well as WordPress plugin file headers:

Is WordPress/developer-plugins-handbook still the source for this page? If so, I'm happy to open a PR with these changes there as well.

body: The [Submitting Your Theme to WordPress.org](https://developer.wordpress.org/themes/releasing-your-theme/submitting-your-theme-to-wordpress-org/) page (last updated 16 September 2024) lacks information about theme naming and external name collision checks. A new theme author might think that checking for a unique name in the WordPress.org directory is enough. However, as the error message states during upload, the system also flags names based on installations outside of WordPress.org. This is not mentioned on the submission page or the "Releasing Your Theme" landing page. What happened I searched the WordPress.org theme directory for my theme name before submitting and found 0 results. I uploaded my theme. The automated scanner rejected the upload, returning this exact error: ERROR: "Qalam" currently has 100+ active installations. Please check for name collisions outside of WordPress.org before approval. I checked online and found the name matched a commercial theme sold on ThemeForest since ~2019. I renamed my theme, and the second upload passed successfully (Reference: https://themes.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/284613). The Gap A directory search showing 0 results is not sufficient because, as the error message states, names are also flagged for installations outside of WordPress.org. The handbook does not tell submitters this before they upload, which can lead to an unexpected rejection. Suggested Solution I suggest updating the page to advise authors on naming checks before they upload. For example, the page could add a note suggesting that authors search the WordPress.org directory and also do a plain web search for their theme name before submitting.

title: [DevHub] Update wp_verify_nonce example to unslash and sanitize input

labels.name: developer documentation (DevHub)
labels.description: Improvements or additions to developer documentation

body:
## Issue Description
The documentation example for `wp_verify_nonce()` shows a nonce value being read directly from `$_POST`. Since `$_POST` contains user-supplied data, the example should follow WordPress coding standards and security recommendations by **unslashing** and **sanitizing** the value before using it.

## URL of the Page with the Issue
[https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/)

## Section of Page with the issue
[Verifying a nonce passed in an AJAX request](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/#verifying-a-nonce-passed-in-an-ajax-request)

## Why is this a problem?
The example code that demonstrates nonce verification accesses `$_POST['my_nonce']` directly:

`wp_verify_nonce( $_POST['my_nonce'], 'process-comment' . $comment_id );`

This does not follow current WordPress coding standards and security recommendations, which advise sanitizing and unslashing user input before use.
Developers often copy examples from the documentation verbatim, so showing direct access to $_POST may unintentionally encourage unsafe patterns.

## Suggested Fix
Sanitizing and unslashing user input before use. 
Suggested update:

`wp_verify_nonce( sanitize_text_field( wp_unslash( $_POST['my_nonce'] ) ), 'process-comment' . $comment_id );`

body: ## Issue Description The Embeds article contains two different changelogs, one that shows changes by WordPress versions and the other that shows updates made to the document itself: The documentation changelog is more up to date than the release version changelog. For example, BlueSky embed was added in [WordPress 6.6](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/61020) and is included in the documentation updates changelog, but not the release changelog above it. ## URL of the Page with the Issue https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/embeds/ ## Section of Page with the issue https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/embeds/#embeds-changelog ## Why is this a problem? Articles should use one documentation changelog to record meaningful updates to the page, such as feature changes, block updates, added or removed services, and major content revisions. The Embeds page currently includes two changelog sections: “Embeds changelog” and “Changelog.” This makes the page harder to maintain because contributors may not know which changelog to update or how the two sections are meant to differ. It also increases the risk that one changelog will be updated while the other becomes outdated. Using one changelog creates a clearer editorial pattern across WordPress documentation. For example, the [Cover block page](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/cover-block/#changelog) uses a single changelog section to document page updates. The Embeds page should follow the same pattern so contributors have one predictable place to record changes. ## Suggested Fix Remove the release changelog and update the table of contents heading to "Changelog" to match other article pages:
